title: House pushes competing veterans’ benefits bills through in unusual votes
summary: Lawmakers passed a bill ending a provision preventing some combat-wounded veterans from collecting both military retirement pay and veterans’ disability compensation as well as a less generous version of that legislation, coupled with billions in other spending cuts.

title: What retirees should know about health insurance during Open Season
summary: Federal retirement benefits expert Tammy Flanagan and Executive Editor Tanya Ballard Brown discuss what federal employees nearing retirement and current retirees should consider when choosing health coverage during Open Season.

title: Lame-duck Congress expedites search for next GAO leader
summary: The last time lawmakers vetted candidates for GAO’s top job, a congressional commission spent more than a year on its search. Now members are being given 24 hours to find candidates in a process top Democrats call a "sham."

summary: At one New Jersey facility, departures left gaps in surgery, wound care and other services. ProPublica found similar disruptions at VA hospitals in three other states.

title: What federal agencies stand to gain by hiring more veterans
summary: COMMENTARY| The IRS has made veteran recruitment a workforce priority. Its chief human capital officer explains why military experience can be an asset across government.

title: Honoring veterans means keeping our promises to them
summary: COMMENTARY | Veterans facing delayed care, disrupted services and long waits for benefits depend on a VA workforce equipped to meet their needs.

title: Feds urge judge to block OPM’s gender affirming care ban
summary: Experts say between 40,000 and 60,000 transgender federal workers have been or will be impacted by the Trump administration's effort to ban coverage of hormone therapies and other gender-affirming treatments.

summary: Despite the Trump administration’s cuts to the civil service, recruiting more early-career workers into agencies has been a bipartisan priority.

title: USPS ‘got the job done’ delivering ballots, as postal unions push to permanently block mail-in voting EO restrictions
summary: A largely self-funded USPS is asking the incoming Democrat-controlled Congress for substantially more funding as the agency looks to avoid running out of cash.

summary: With a new Congress in 2027, companies could see more anti-corruption probes.

summary: Several government oversight reports have found that agencies made costly operational errors as they implemented the administration’s cost-cutting directives.

summary: From FEHB eligibility rules to Medicare enrollment deadlines, the right steps before your last day can protect coverage for you and your spouse.

summary: The Arthur S. Flemming awards have been around for more than 75 years and generally recognize civil servants who work in scientific fields.

summary: A House committee's top Democrat is reminding agency heads to preserve all records, as the party draws up its post-midterms oversight plans.
